subject: Embeddings integration migration - next steps

Subject: Embeddings integration migration - next steps

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Recap:
- Use case: semantic search + reranking for product docs + FAQ retrieval across multi-lingual content.
- Current provider: vendor-X embeddings (1536-dim) used for search index.
- Primary concerns: latency at peak QPS, cost per 1M embeddings, and vector normalization differences causing score drift.

Proposed next steps (POC scope):
1) Technical validation: we'll run a small re-embedding job (sample 50k docs) to compare recall and cost across model variants.
2) Migration strategy: export existing vectors + source docs; run re-embedding vs translation path test to confirm parity.
3) Integration/architecture follow-ups: SDK setup, auth, routing, and structured output for reranker.
4) Performance tuning: batching recommendations, normalization (L2 vs cosine pre-normalize), and recommended vector dims.

Action items for Acme:
- Share a representative dataset (5k–10k docs) and current scoring examples (top10 queries).
- Confirm target throughput (QPS) and SLO for tail latency.

What we'll deliver before the POC call:
- Migration plan (attached PDF) with timeline, cost estimate, and rollback steps.
- Sample reindex script (sample-embed-reindex.sh) and SDK snippet for quick start.

Technical notes (short):
- Vector dimensions: we can support 1536 to match vendor-X for parity; we also recommend testing 768 and 1024 for cost/quality trade-offs. Many customers see similar retrieval quality at 768 for document-level retrieval, but KB/semantic nuance sometimes benefits from 1024+ depending on the model and chunking.
- Batching: for embeddings bulk reindex jobs we suggest 512–4096 items per batch depending on instance memory; for online calls target 64–512 depending on latency SLO.
- Normalization: we recommend L2-normalizing embeddings post-generation for cosine similarity stability. If you currently store unnormalized vectors, we'll include a normalization step in the reindex job.
- Auth: SDK uses API keys by default; for Private deployments we support mTLS and KMS-backed keys.
- Routing: you can route requests to a dedicated embeddings pool for consistent latency; we'll include a routing policy for canary traffic during migration.

Next call: can we schedule a 60-min technical POC on Wed 9/15? I'll include Vivek (solutions) and Rishi (SRE) to review the reindex plan.

Attaching: redwood-embed-migration-plan.pdf, sample-embed-reindex.sh

Thanks,

Jordan — great questions. Answering inline and adding a few implementation details so your engineers have something to start with.

> 1) We're currently on 1536-dim vectors. If we test 768, do you expect a measurable drop in retrieval quality for our product-doc use case? Any rule of thumb?

Short answer: usually small to moderate depending on chunk size and query complexity. Rule-of-thumb: 
- 768 dims: often sufficient for document-level semantic search where chunks are ~200–500 tokens.
- 1024–1536: helpful for fine-grained similarity (short snippets, paraphrase-heavy queries).

We recommend running an A/B on a sample set: re-embed 10k docs at 768 and 1536, run your top 100 queries, and compare recall@10 and MRR. We'll help with scripts to automate this.

> 2) For reindexing, can you confirm whether Redwood will generate new IDs or accept our existing vector IDs (we'd prefer to keep current doc IDs for back-compatibility).

We support preserving your existing doc IDs. The sample script (attached) accepts an optional id field and will upsert vectors into your embeddings index. If you prefer a blue/green approach we can also create a new index and swap aliases after validation.

Implementation details for your engineers:
- SDK quickstart (python):

``
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient(api_key="<REPLACE>")
vecs = client.embed.batch(texts, model="rw-embed-1", batch_size=1024, normalize=True)
client.index.upsert(index_name="acme-products-v1", items=[{"id": doc_id, "vector": v} for doc_id,v in enumerate(vecs)])
``

Notes: batch_size and normalize flags as shown. The normalize=True option will L2-normalize before upload.

- Auth & routing: for the POC you can use API keys scoped to the embeddings index. If you move to Dedicated or Private, we'll provision a dedicated pool and provide mTLS certs + KMS integration. We also support routing rules so traffic for reindex jobs goes to high-throughput capacity while online queries hit lower-latency pools.

- Reranker pattern: keep a two-stage pipeline: retrieve (FAISS/HNSW on normalized vectors) -> lightweight reranker (structured output / tool-calling) for final score. Redwood supports structured tool-calls from the SDK to call your domain-specific scoring function during rerank.

- Batching guidance:
  - Bulk reindex: 1k–4k per batch if you have machines with 64GB+ RAM.
  - Online embedding calls: 64–256 for sub-100ms p95 depending on model and region.

Proposed POC agenda (60m):
- 10m: goals + success metrics
- 20m: embed sample run (we'll demo reindex on a small sample)
- 20m: discuss routing/rollout and rollback plan
- 10m: next steps & timeline

I've attached the migration plan and a sample reindex script. Vivek — can you prepare a short runbook for alias swap and rollback steps we can share in the call? Rishi — please bring the expected infra cost numbers for 50k and 500k doc reindex.

Thanks — looking forward to the POC. Wed 9/15 1:30pm PST works from our side; sending calendar invite now.
